uses: Ginger has been part of folk medicine since ancient times. The warming root is traditionally taken for indigestion, wind and queasy stomachs, including travel sickness, and hot ginger tea is a common household drink at the start of a cold. Culpeper praised it for warming the stomach and stiff joints. A ginger rub or compress was once used to bring warmth and redness to the skin over aching areas.
energetics: Culpeper called ginger hot and dry in the second degree
caution_pregnancy: NCCIH says ginger supplements may be safe in pregnancy but advises talking with a health care provider first. The EMA notes reassuring data from several hundred pregnancies yet still advises avoiding medicinal ginger in pregnancy as a precaution. Safety while breastfeeding hasn't been established; little is known.
caution_medications: Evidence is mixed. Case reports describe people on the blood thinner warfarin whose blood became much thinner (high INR) after starting ginger supplements, though a small study in healthy men found no effect. If you take warfarin or another blood thinner, talk with your prescriber before using ginger supplements. The EMA lists no known interactions.
caution_conditions: Can cause stomach upset, burping, heartburn, nausea, diarrhea and mouth or throat irritation. Avoid it if you are allergic to ginger. The EMA does not support most medicinal uses under age 18. Joint pain with swelling, redness or fever should be checked by a doctor.
caution_duration: The EMA advises seeing a practitioner if digestive symptoms last more than two weeks, joint pain more than four weeks, or cold symptoms more than a week. None of our sources sets a long-term limit.
caution_topical: Ginger warms and reddens the skin, and allergic reactions are reported; keep it off broken or sensitive skin and test a small area first.
garden_harvest_timing: Dig young tender ginger about four to five months after planting; mature rhizomes about seven months after planting, as the leaves die back.
garden_sun: Partial shade in hot climates; full sun where summers are cool
garden_water: Evenly moist but never soggy; stop watering container plants while dormant
notes: A tropical plant: it needs warm soil to grow and goes dormant in the cold. In cold climates grow it in a pot and bring it indoors when nights fall below about 50°F. Store rhizomes for replanting in a cool, dry place, not the refrigerator. Culpeper lists ginger among his simples but gives it no planet.
